title: Titus (the emperor)
lead: Titus, son of Vespasian, who finished the Jewish war by taking Jerusalem and destroying the Temple in AD 70, then reigned as emperor from 79 to 81. Not Paul's coworker Titus, whose page is the topic titus.

sections.b: Tacitus says Vespasian sent his son Titus to pay respects to Galba (1:10). Josephus adds that Agrippa sailed with him and that, hearing in Greece that Galba was dead, Titus turned back and came to his father at Caesarea (Jewish War 4.9.2). Wikipedia gives his birth as 30 December AD 39, the capture of Jerusalem and destruction of the Second Temple in AD 70, and his reign as 24 June 79 to 13 September 81. Tacitus names him among those who advanced his career (1:1).
sections.refs: Histories of Tacitus 1:1; Histories of Tacitus 1:10

sections.b: Paul's coworker Titus (Galatians 2:1-5; Titus 1:5) is a different man, a Gentile Christian. The two share only a common Latin name.
